correctness.rationale: Equality of two deletion histories iff x[t]=x[t+b] throughout the intervening interval proves interval convexity of valid starts. Endpoint intersection sizes are q^(b-d) for d<=b, and a unique period-b indicator for d>b. Each output with h histories contributes (h-s+1)_+ to T_s, so second differences reconstruct each N_s, including m=0 and terminal zero conventions. Uniform vertex labels on the b disjoint comparison paths give independent equality indicators, hence expected counts and longest-run law; standard union/block bounds establish log_q m scaling at fixed b,q. Fresh literal enumerations checked 1,281 fixed-center parameter cases, not an infinite proof.

evidence: Lan et al. Theorem III.2 gives q^(b-1)(1+(m+1)(q-1)) for one burst; Xi et al. address same-length deletion-then-insertion ball sizes.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The former is the sum of N_s; a scalar sum does not imply the full multiplicity histogram, and the latter uses a different channel.
